 Updated: 7:01 PM PST Nov 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ophelia Young Meteorologist Clouds increase Sunday night, setting the stage for a cool, overcast but dry Monday. On Election Day, rain chances arrive in the Valley by midmorning before the progressive front reaches the foothills around lunchtime. 
 Isolated thunderstorms are possible in the Sierra Tuesday afternoon. 
 Dry weather returns for the rest of the week, with partly cloudy skies, light north winds and Valley highs gradually reaching the low 70s. 
 Advertisement Hearst Owned Monday forecast
 Most of the region will walk out to mostly cloudy skies by Monday morning. Patchy fog is also possible. 
 Despite the cloud cover, Monday will remain dry, with overcast skies keeping temperatures cool.
 Hearst Owned Storms systems arrives Election Day
 The clouds are increasing ahead of our next weather system. 
 It will push a quick-moving cold front through the region on Tuesday, which happens to be Election Day. 
 The wettest impacts will be in the Sacramento Valley, northern foothills and northern Sierra.
 Hearst Owned Timing of showers
 Timing can change as the system draws closer. 
 Right now forecast models suggest rain chances reach the Valley by Tuesday midmorning. 
 Showers climb into the foothills around lunchtime, with isolated thunderstorms possible in the Sierra by afternoon. 
A second wave of light showers is possible late Tuesday evening. 
 Advertisement Hearst Owned Dry rest of week
 Dry weather returns for the rest of the week, with temperatures returning to seasonal normal by the upcoming weekend.
 Hearst Owned Foothills and Sierra 7 day forecast
 Those headed out in foothills and Sierra on Tuesday should prepare for a few showers. 
 In the Sierra, winds will also be breezy and rain will turn into snow above 7000 feet. 
 Hearst Owned Valley 7 day forecast
 The region dries out Tuesday night and the rest of the week will be partly cloudy with light winds. 
 The mild weather will stretch into the upcoming weekend.
